title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the previous page: Grothendieck has written a group M_{0,3}~ as a semidirect product Ŝ^+_{0,3} · Π_σ~.
- The normal factor Ŝ^+_{0,3} is identified with SL(2,Z)^, the profinite completion of SL(2,Z), i.e. the profinite fundamental group of the modular orbifold.
- Π_σ~ is a group of 'operators' u. From the cocycle formulas these are Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type elements, attached to the order-4 (j=1728) vertex σ.
- On SL(2,Z)^ he has the canonical map φ'_0 : SL(2,Z)^ → SL(2,Ẑ)' ⊂ GL(2,Ẑ)'.
- On Π_σ~ he has a map φ'_σ(u) = μ(tσ_∞ + u)τ_∞^ε = μ[[u, εt], [−t, εu]], with t, u ∈ Ẑ, μ ∈ Ẑ*, ε = (−1)^α.
- Since σ_∞ is the order-4 rotation, tσ_∞ + u is a Gaussian integer in Ẑ[i]. Since τ_∞ acts as conjugation, φ'_σ lands in the normalizer of the non-split 'Gaussian' Cartan Ẑ[i]* in GL2(Ẑ).
- He defines φ'(a·u) = φ'_0(a)φ'_σ(u).

This page:
- Theorem: φ' is a group homomorphism.
- Because φ'_0 is already a homomorphism and the group is a semidirect product, this is equivalent to two statements:
  - (8) φ'_σ is a homomorphism on Π_σ~;
  - (9) the compatibility φ'_0(u a u^{-1}) = φ'_σ(u) φ'_0(a) φ'_σ(u)^{-1}.
- Proof of the equivalence: expand φ'(a u a' u') = φ'(a · (u a' u^{-1}) · u u').
- He notes that (9) holds by construction: the matrix φ'_σ(u) was built in earlier paragraphs (formulas (67), (68), corollary to Th. (77)) precisely so that conjugation by u on SL(2,Z)^ is matched by conjugation by φ'_σ(u). So only (8) remains.
- To prove (8) he first records how the invariants g, h, f of a product u'u are expressed through those of u', u. These are the 'cocycle relations' (10):
  - g(u'u) = u'(g(u)) · g(u');
  - h(u'u) = u'(h(u)^{±1}) · h(u');
  - f(u'u) = f(u') · u'(f(u)).
- The last relation is exactly the composition law of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group: (λ1, f1)(λ2, f2) = (λ1λ2, f1 · F1(f2)).
- On the next page these cocycles are pushed into GL(2,Ẑ)' and combined with the cocycles α, β, to compute t, u, μ, ε of a product and so verify multiplicativity.

Overall aim: construct a continuous homomorphism from a GT/Teichmüller-type extension of SL(2,Z)^ into GL2(Ẑ). It extends the canonical map on SL(2,Z)^, and on the stabilizer of the j=1728 point it has 'CM by Z[i]' shape. It is a combinatorial analogue of Galois acting on the Tate module of the CM curve y² = x³ − x.
errors: In (9) the last factor appears as φ'_σ(u^{-1})^{-1} (or a similar variant). For a conjugation formula it should be φ'_σ(u)^{-1}, or equivalently φ'_σ(u^{-1}) once (8) is known; this is probably a slip.
Part b) writes Γ_σ / Π_σ without the tilde, while a) uses Π_σ~; this is a notational inconsistency.

The exponent on h(u) in the second cocycle relation is uncertain (possibly an inverse); Remark 2 on the next page discusses replacing g, h by their inverses. The precise form cannot be checked from this page alone.
The proof of (8) is only announced here ('un calcul immédiat'); the verification is deferred to the following pages.

ideas.what: Reducing 'φ' is a homomorphism on a semidirect product' to φ'_σ being a homomorphism plus a conjugation-equivariance condition
ideas.modern_name: homomorphisms out of a semidirect product

ideas.what: Composition law for the f-component of GT-type operators: f(u'u) = f(u')·u'(f(u))
ideas.modern_name: group law of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT^ (1-cocycle relation)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the Teichmüller tower; the explicit cocycle form is in Drinfeld and Ihara

ideas.what: A homomorphism from an extension SL(2,Z)^ ⋊ Π_σ~ to GL2(Ẑ), which on the stabilizer of the order-4 vertex takes values in the normalizer of the Gaussian Cartan μ(u + tσ_∞)τ^ε
ideas.modern_name: GT-type action on the genus-1 / M_{1,1} level, with a CM-type (Z[i]) representation at the j=1728 point; analogue of the Galois representation on the Tate module of y² = x³ − x
ideas.usually_credited_to: Genus-1 GT: Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura, Enriquez (elliptic associators); CM Galois representations: Deuring, Serre–Tate
ideas.where_published: Possibly prefigured in La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981); unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck builds an explicit homomorphism into GL2(Ẑ) from a GT-type group of operators attached to the order-4 point σ, combined with SL(2,Z)^. On the stabilizer of σ it has the shape of a non-split (Gaussian) Cartan normalizer. This purely combinatorial 'GT → GL2(Ẑ) with CM by Z[i] at j=1728' map, proved homomorphic via the cocycle relations of g, h, f, does not appear in this explicit form in the published genus-1 GT literature as far as I know.
missed.quote: Théorème L'application φ' est un homomorphisme de groupes.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could give a GT-theoretic (Galois-free) construction of the CM-type 'Tate module' character at j=1728. This is relevant to the open question of how far GT^ mimics Gal(Q̄/Q) in genus 1, and to the elliptic-associator theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly a formal reduction plus standard GT cocycle relations. The interest lies in the surrounding construction, a GT-type extension mapping to GL2(Ẑ) through a Gaussian Cartan, which seems only partially reflected in the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Ĝ^+_{0,3}' should read 𝔖̂^+_{0,3} (script S, as on the previous page).
'φ_0 est déjà' is φ'_0 (with prime) in context.
The exponent on τ_∞ is ε (the transcription has ξ).
'u', u'' ∈ M_{0,3}~' should probably read u', u ∈ M_{0,3}~ (the second u is unprimed).
